clue.text: Ambassador behind ceremonial transport

parts.note: an ambassador is styled His Excellency, abbreviated HE
behind means the backside, slangily the arse

explanation.surface: A diplomat rides at the back of some stately procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word but is a noun for the rear end; ARSE is British slang for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin in a funeral procession, a solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Ripped up vacuous exam over a rhetorical question

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ripped means tore

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word exam remain

explanation.surface: A student tears up a pointless exam paper over some unanswerable question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TORE into EROT; 'vacuous' empties EXAM to EM; 'over' places these above A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotema is the rhetorician's term for a question asked for effect, not expecting an answer.

clue.text: Looking back in some secret rooms

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces in hidden chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the past, so it is backward-looking.

clue.text: Order to ignore the port?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship; a parade-ground command to turn heads to the right in effect ignores the left

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to touch the after-dinner port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the fortified wine or a harbour, but here it is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: This military command makes marching troops turn their heads to the right, away from the left side.

clue.text: Hoi polloi split by army regulars, by the way

parts.note: rent is a past form of rend, so split or torn

indicators.note: regulars picks regularly spaced letters, here the first and third of army

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation of obiter, Latin for by the way or incidentally

explanation.surface: The common masses are divided by professional soldiers, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army regulars' looks like career soldiers but picks alternate letters, A and M. OB for obiter is a less familiar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd hired to protest, loosely the rabble or common people.

clue.text: Let back in US college for supporting study

indicators.note: supporting means sitting beneath, holding up the other piece in a down entry

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An American college backs a research project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts MIT below READ in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to allow them entry again.

clue.text: Having more of these, you must want more

definitions.text: Having more of these, you must want more

parts.words: Having more of these, you must want more
parts.note: a riddle: the more requirements you have, the more you lack and want, playing on the saying about must

explanation.surface: A paradox about greed: the more you have, the more you crave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' here means lack: having more requirements means wanting more things, echoing the proverb 'needs must'.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are things you lack and so want; each extra one adds to what you desire.

clue.text: Material complaint following infection deaths reported among drivers

indicators.note: among says the pieces sit inside the outer word

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation for drivers
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
flu is a common viral infection

indicators.note: reported says the word is taken as heard spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: deaths are ends

explanation.surface: A medical report about people catching a disease from motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns ENDS into a sound-alike spelt ENZ; 'among' puts the pieces inside the initials of the Automobile Association, a British motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluenza is the jocular malaise of the wealthy: obsession with possessions, a materialistic ailment.

clue.text: Unobtrusively 'discovered' another oddball heading Question Time

indicators.note: heading means the first part goes on top of the next, in a down entry
oddball signals that the letters are arranged in a strange way
dis-covered means with its covering removed, so only the inside letters of another remain

parts.note: QT abbreviates Question Time, the BBC political debate programme

explanation.surface: Another eccentric quietly fronts a political TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips ANOTHER to NOTHE, which 'oddball' rearranges as ONTHE. Question Time is a BBC debate programme.
explanation.definitionFit: On the quiet, often written on the QT, means secretly or without drawing attention.

clue.text: Apparently where trap is centrepiece in terrorist attack

parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth, which is on the face

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a word is its single middle letter, here of terrorist

parts.note: a fit is an attack of illness

explanation.surface: A bomb-plot story: where a trap is the key element in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap is slang for the mouth. 'centrepiece in' takes O, the middle letter of TERRORIST.
explanation.definitionFit: On the face of it means judging by appearances, seemingly.

clue.text: Make bad blood when reflecting on a quick communication

indicators.note: on means placed after, so these letters follow the next piece
reflecting as in a mirror means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or make bad
gore is spilled blood

explanation.surface: Someone causes ill feeling by thinking about a brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when reflecting' reverses MARGORE into EROGRAM, and 'on a' puts that after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogram is a lightweight airmail letter, a fast way of sending a written message abroad.

clue.text: Maybe Oxford manufacturer is stronger, having exported the first ton

indicators.note: exported says a letter is sent out of the word, and the first says which occurrence

parts.note: stouter means sturdier or stronger

explanation.surface: A boast that some Oxford firm is mightier after shipping its first ton abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a lace-up shoe, not the city; souter is an old Scots word for a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A souter is a cobbler, and an Oxford is a style of shoe he might make.

clue.text: Knife found in pub just after midnight?

parts.note: a bar is a pub
on means just after, as in on the hour
the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A blade turns up in a pub soon after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as the middle of NIGHT, giving G.
explanation.definitionFit: A barong is a broad-bladed knife or machete used in the Philippines.

clue.text: Method of choice covering specific period

indicators.note: covering says one word wraps around the other

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a particular period of time

explanation.surface: A procedure for choosing that applies to a given time frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a way of working or procedure, a method of doing something.

clue.text: Becoming fond of rebuke that ousts Left

indicators.note: ousts means throws out, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a talking-to is a scolding or rebuke

explanation.surface: Warming to a reprimand that throws out the political Left.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to someone is to start liking them.

clue.text: Woman's disgusted about losing Charlie's delivery of smack

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped
about signals turning the letters round

parts.note: Margo is a woman's name, with the possessive S
sick means disgusted, as in sick of
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman is revolted by a delivery of heroin after losing her dealer Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses MARGOS SICK to KCISSOGRAM; 'losing' drops C. Smack looks like heroin but means a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A kissogram is a greeting delivered with a kiss, a smacker, by a hired messenger.

clue.text: Drunk embracing the setter has to go on a spree

indicators.note: embracing says the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: lit up is slang for drunk
the setter says I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A tipsy setter admits needing to go out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: IVE is inserted into LIT UP after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To live it up is to enjoy yourself extravagantly, a binge of fun.

clue.text: One will cut devious histrionics from five onwards?

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters are rearranged
from five onwards means the word is used only from its fifth letter, so its first four letters go

explanation.surface: Someone will curb melodramatic acting from five o'clock onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from five onwards' leaves RIONICS, which 'devious' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front tooth whose job is cutting food.

clue.text: Did groom feign missing tango when touring Spain?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened word surrounds the other letter
missing means a letter is left out

parts.note: to feign is to pretend
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Did a bridegroom fake a dance-free honeymoon round Spain?
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops T from PRETEND; 'when touring' puts PREEND around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to groom oneself, so preened is the past tense of grooming.

clue.text: Closely follow pretence circulating these days

indicators.note: circulating means going around the other letters

parts.note: a show is a pretence, as in a show of concern
AD, anno Domini, denotes the present era

explanation.surface: Tailing a sham that is doing the rounds nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them secretly.

clue.text: Musicians so-so — bit patchy

indicators.note: patchy means uneven or irregular, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A review of some players: mediocre, a little inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patchy' rearranges SOSO and BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboists are players of the oboe, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Month to get brown in 45 degrees

indicators.note: in says the colour goes inside the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Getting a suntan in a month when it is 45 degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: '45 degrees' looks like hot weather but is an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is an eighth of a circle, an arc of 45 degrees.

clue.text: Half-hearted regime overthrown, broken by power

indicators.note: broken by says the other letter splits this word
overthrown means turned over, so the word is read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a diet is a regime of eating

explanation.surface: A lukewarm regime toppled by those holding power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' reverses DIET to TEID, and 'broken by' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid support is lukewarm or unenthusiastic.

clue.text: Caught cutting ecstasy, say ; – ) ?

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the other word

parts.note: ecstasy is an example of a strong feeling, an emotion
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed cutting a pill of the drug, with a winking face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' suggests the drug or E, but is an example of a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A winking face typed in punctuation marks is an emoticon.

clue.text: Mostly mischievous war parties

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: impish means mischievous

explanation.surface: Mainly naughty raiding parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Impis were Zulu regiments, armed bands of warriors.

clue.text: Cords for making jumpers fit

parts.note: jumpers looks like knitted sweaters and cords like trousers, but the jumpers are people exercising

explanation.surface: Clothing advice: corduroys and sweaters that fit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a sweater and cords are corduroy trousers; here the jumpers leap and fit means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes swung over the head for leaping are a classic fitness training tool.

clue.text: Single nest spotted in run around island

indicators.note: spotted in means seen placed inside
around signals the letters turned back to front

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
I, the Roman numeral, is one
a nid is a pheasant's nest

explanation.surface: A lone nest seen during a run round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the run word back to front as TRAD; a nid is a pheasant's nest, an uncommon word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Waste energy on half-hearted wife

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y means X comes after Y, so energy's letter is attached to the end
half-hearted removes half of the heart, one of the two central S letters

parts.note: missus is informal for wife
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Squandering energy on an unenthusiastic wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one S of MISSUS's double-S heart; 'on' puts E after.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse something is to use it wrongly, to squander it.
